subject: Oakcrest: private/on-prem feasibility & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private hosting for Oakcrest pilot — high level ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up with our security and infra teams and there are two hard constraints: all PHI processing must occur inside our VPC (no egress to shared hosted endpoints) and the ability to run inference on a set of on-prem servers for pre-production workloads.

Can Redwood run a small pilot that: 
- deploys your control plane in a private org VPC (customer-managed)
- runs inference on an on-prem GPU node behind our firewall via a connector
- provides audit logs and key management integration (we use Vault + HSM)

We appreciate a short feasibility note (high-level architecture and any constraints) plus a rough timeline and resource asks so we can brief procurement and engineering.

--
Emma Lawson
Director, Digital Transformation
Oakcrest Medical
emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting for Oakcrest pilot — high level ask

Emma — thanks, and totally understood on the PHI constraints. Looping in product, infra, and CS to scope a concrete proposal.

Quick notes we’ll include in the feasibility:
- Two deployment modes: (A) Private control plane (Redwood control plane runs in customer VPC) + on-prem runtime connector; (B) Full on-prem variant (control plane packaged for customer infra).
- Minimum infra for connector pilot: 1x A40 / A100-class node with 32+ GB RAM for the model family you showed; ephemeral test load only.
- Security: we support KMS integrations and can bind logs to a customer-managed S3/Blob. HSM integration will need an engineering spike.

Marissa — can you draft the pilot runbook and highlight any product limitations (function calling, streaming, KV cache behavior) for an on-prem connector?
Karthik — can you validate the minimum node specs and give an initial effort estimate for the connector + HSM work?
Soojin — need a quick ops feasibility: who needs to be on-call and what access patterns to expect.
Jordan — I’ll flag CS for onboarding and success criteria.

Emma — we’ll aim to return a short feasibility doc + timeline by EOD Friday. If procurement needs a placeholder cost band we can include an estimated number for pilot effort.

—Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting for Oakcrest pilot — high level ask

Thanks Priyom — attaching a first-pass runbook (see attachment) and a short notes sheet. High-level product caveats: 
- Function/tool calling and streaming: both work over the connector but latency will vary; heavy streaming at low-latency SLAs will need dedicated capacity.
- KV cache: persisted KV cache must live on the runtime host; for the pilot we can accept warm caches only.
- Model variants: we can ship a quantized variant if Oakcrest wants lower-cost on-prem inference, but we’ll need to validate quality against your prompts.

Pilot success criteria (proposed):
1) End-to-end inference over connector with <150ms median per-token processing for standard flows under test load.
2) All audit logs forwarded to Oakcrest-controlled bucket for 30-day retention.
3) Vault-based key retrieval for model keys (baseline HSM integration optional for pilot).

Open product questions:
- Does Oakcrest require the control plane to be fully air-gapped (no outbound to Redwood) or is private control plane in their VPC acceptable?
- Expected peak concurrency during the pilot (helps us size connector).

--Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting for Oakcrest pilot — high level ask

Folks — did a quick infra sketch and effort estimate. Summary: 
- Connector approach (preferred for a fast pilot): Redwood runtime in a lightweight container on your on-prem host + gRPC tunnel to control plane inside your VPC. Effort: 2 weeks engineering + 1 week validation with Oakcrest (2-3 engineers, part-time).
- Full on-prem control plane (air-gapped) is feasible but is a heavier lift: 6-8 weeks and requires additional packaging/testing (3-4 engineers, full-time) and a minimal on-call rotation.
- HSM integration: priority spike of ~5 engineering days to prove PKCS#11 flow; production-grade HSM support likely 3-4 weeks of engineering work.

Node sizing: for the 13B encoder-decoder family Oakcrest used in demo, a single A40 or equivalent (48GB VRAM preferred) will handle baseline pilot traffic with batching tuned. If Oakcrest wants redundancy for failover add a second node.

Security notes: the gRPC tunnel must be initiated from within Oakcrest (outbound) if firewalls restrict inbound. Mutual TLS and client certs will be required.

I’ll attach the infra sketch to the shared Drive.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@oakcrestmed.com <procurement@oakcrestmed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@oakcrestmed.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T14:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Oakcrest pilot — procurement and timelines

Hi Priyom / Emma,

Procurement here. To proceed we need:
- A scoped statement of work for the pilot (deliverables, timeline, acceptance criteria).
- Placeholder cost estimate for the pilot and an outline of potential ongoing pricing if we decide to adopt dedicated private hosting.
- Standard security docs: SOC2 attestation (or equivalent), data processing addendum, and that audit logs will be stored in our bucket.

Can Redwood provide a one-page SOW and preliminary cost band by next Wednesday (2026-10-13)? Also, if there are any vendor approvals needed (e.g., DataSafe connector), include that in the SOW.

Thanks,
Oakcrest Procurement
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, procurement@oakcrestmed.com
Date: 2026-10-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Oakcrest: private/on-prem feasibility & pilot proposal

Procurement / Emma — thanks for the clarity. Quick internal summary and decision ask:

Summary of what we can commit for a pilot (connector model):
- Deliverables: private control plane deployed into Oakcrest VPC, runtime connector on one customer node (A40-class), Vault-based key retrieval configured, audit logs delivered to Oakcrest S3 path, basic runbook + run-of-test.
- Timeline: SOW + cost band by 2026-10-13; engineering spike (2 weeks) and pilot run (2 weeks) — total calendar ~6 weeks after SOW sign.
- Cost band (placeholder): $45k–$70k for pilot engineering and support (depends on HSM work and node redundancy). Ongoing pricing dependent on committed throughput and support tier.
- Risks/reqs: HSM full integration extends schedule by ~3–4 weeks; if Oakcrest requires fully air-gapped control plane we must move to a full on-prem package (6–8 week delivery).

Decision ask for Redwood leadership: approve scoping the pilot under a standard pilot SOW and allocate 2 engineers (part-time) + 1 infra SME (Karthik) and 1 product lead (Marissa) for project coordination. We also request approval for a possible 3-week HSM spike should Oakcrest insist on HSM in pilot. Estimated burn in that case moves to top of cost band.

If leadership signs off I’ll draft the SOW and an internal resourcing calendar and share by EOD Wednesday.

--Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
